ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

CYP2D6 inhibition

A 29-year-old woman has tolerated atomoxetine for several months. After fluoxetine is added, she develops prominent tachycardia and nausea without a change in atomoxetine dose. Which pharmacokinetic mechanism most plausibly increases atomoxetine exposure?

  1. Reduced intestinal absorption through chelation
  2. Accelerated renal elimination of unchanged atomoxetine
  3. Increased first-pass metabolism of atomoxetine
  4. Inhibition of CYP2D6-mediated metabolism
  5. Induction of CYP2D6-mediated metabolism
Answer and explanation

Inhibition of CYP2D6-mediated metabolism

A strong CYP2D6 inhibitor can increase atomoxetine concentrations and may require a dosing review.

Option explanations

Inhibition of CYP2D6-mediated metabolism: A strong CYP2D6 inhibitor can increase atomoxetine concentrations and may require a dosing review.

Induction of CYP2D6-mediated metabolism: Induction would usually reduce exposure to an active substrate.

Reduced intestinal absorption through chelation: This would reduce exposure rather than account for increased adverse effects.

Accelerated renal elimination of unchanged atomoxetine: Enhanced elimination would lower concentrations.

Increased first-pass metabolism of atomoxetine: This would tend to decrease systemic availability.
